Symptom: PC1 cannot reach the server at 192.168.20.100.
Topology_Note: PC1 is connected to SW1. SW1 connects to R1. R1 connects to SW2, where the server is connected.
Show_Output: show ip interface brief: G0/0 192.168.10.1 up/up; G0/1 192.168.20.1 up/up. PC1 ping to 192.168.20.100: 100% packet loss.
Expected_Fault: PC1 is configured with an incorrect default gateway. The configured gateway is 192.168.10.254, while R1 G0/0 is 192.168.10.1.

Symptom: PC1 cannot reach the server at 192.168.20.100
Topology_Note: PC1 is connected to SW1, which connects to R1 G0/0
Expected_Fault: PC1 has an IP address belonging to the wrong network.

Symptom: PC1 cannot reach the gateway or server.
Topology_Note: PC1 is connected to SW1, which connects to R1 G0/0.
Expected_Fault: PC1 has an incorrect subnet mask, causing the configured gateway to be outside PC1's calculated subnet.

Symptom: PC1 and PC2 experience unreliable communication on the LAN.

Expected_Fault: PC1 and PC2 are configured with the same IPv4 address, creating an IP address conflict.
